Leading UK financial services provider Quilter innovates to drive performance improvements, enhance customer experience, and deliver on ambitious efficiency targets while sustaining growth.
Jeremy Mugridge, Marketing Director, Quilter

Quilter is a leading financial services company headquartered in the United Kingdom, renowned for its comprehensive wealth management solutions. The Quilter team was eager to explore what AI and, in particular, generative AI, could deliver for the business, its people, its operations, and its clients and began exploring Microsoft Copilot.

David Reynolds explains, “Copilot is heavily integrated into the whole Microsoft product suite and, of course, when a product is simple and well-integrated, we will be more interested in delivering it. There is less cost and effort on our side; it costs us less to administer the whole estate. But for me, the most important aspect is the security and granularity of control.”

“With Microsoft, we know that our data remains in our control, that has been really positive for us,” David Reynolds adds. “Copilot offers a secure platform. Microsoft’s robust data protection policies and the assurances it provides regarding data privacy are key factors in our decision to use Copilot.”
Leveraging Microsoft’s Early Adoption Programme, Quilter rolled out the integration in phases, beginning with the technology department.

Licences were swapped frequently across the department so that many people had an opportunity to experiment with Copilot during the pilot phase. This was extended to include marketing, investment, legal, HR, and finance teams.

“We distributed the licences and asked the teams to really play around with the tools,” explains Alex Krupa. “We gave everyone 20 or 30 suggestions for potential ways to use Copilot, but also encouraged everyone to think about how they could integrate Copilot into their professional lives in ways we perhaps wouldn’t have thought of.”

Quilter adopted an approach that gave individuals the flexibility to innovate. Dedicated Microsoft Teams channels enabled people to share their experiences, tips, and tricks. Quilter leant into the support from Microsoft to provide targeting training sessions.

“Our biggest use case has been meetings and transcriptions,” acknowledges David Reynolds. “But I am keen to explore more novel use cases. Our second biggest use case is using Copilot as a starter for document creation. For example, Copilot is great at helping to write job descriptions and end-of-year appraisals.”
Embraced by the marketing team
“I’m probably one of the biggest fans of Copilot in the business,” admits Jeremy Mugridge, Marketing Director at Quilter. “I’ve already seen use cases that have got me quite excited!”
The team at Quilter is now using Copilot to automate repetitive tasks, improve efficiency, and transform workflows across the organisation.

“A big part of the way we go about our audit activity involves the use of innovative technologies,” says Alex Krupa. “We’re trying to move away from sampling small numbers to providing assurance with full population testing. With the right controls and tooling, generative AI is helping us on that journey as part of a wider internal audit innovation and data analytics strategy.”
In addition to enabling this ambitious new approach to internal auditing, the audit team has been busy exploring other use cases for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

He continues, “Our work also often involves the aggregation of a lot of data; strategy papers, board reports, etc. We use Copilot to aggregate the information and present an initial review. This way, it helps to make our work more efficient.”
Quilter is investing in helping its people develop the prompting skills they need to realise the potential of Copilot.

“I hope our deployment of Copilot will encourage people to want to work here,” says Jeremy Mugridge. “They will see us as a forward-thinking, technology-driven company and I would hope that will attract a higher calibre of person. We can help people get up to speed with prompting but also they can use Copilot to upskill themselves and fill in any gaps in their skillset.”

Providing employees with Microsoft 365 Copilot has been a cornerstone of Quilter’s strategy to foster productivity and confidence. By equipping teams with this powerful tool, the organisation has empowered employees to approach challenges with greater creativity.

生成AIがハードウェア設計にもたらす変革：Quilterの事例に見る「物理世界の自動化」と日本企業の勝機
テキストや画像の生成にとどまらず、物理法則や厳密なルールが求められるエンジニアリング領域におけるAI活用の可能性と、日本の「モノづくり」産業への示唆を解説します
日本は電子機器、自動車、ロボティクスといったハードウェア産業に強みを持ちますが、同時に「熟練設計者の高齢化」と「人手不足」という深刻な課題に直面しています
また、日本企業特有の「品質へのこだわり」とAIの親和性も無視できません
今回の事例を踏まえ、日本の製造業やハードウェア関連企業が検討すべきポイントを整理します
日本の商習慣上、最終承認プロセス（デザインレビュー）の重要性は変わらないどころか、より多角的な視点が必要になります
日本企業に多い「暗黙知」や「あうんの呼吸」で行われていた設計ノウハウを、AIが理解可能な形式知（明確なルールセット）に落とし込む作業が、AI導入の最初のステップとなります
